claims.statement: For the full protected BN254 target and uniform z=g^x, the concrete one-trial 32-adding Pollard-rho algorithm, can return P0 and [x]Q0 with e(P0,[x]Q0)=z with exploratory success probability at least 0.40, using at most 2^134.353770 reference units (20,000 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents per unit) and at most 2^20 bytes of peak total storage on one processor. The success assessment relies on the disclosed standard r-adding collision-time heuristic, supported and limited as explained in proof.md; it is not an unconditional production success theorem. Total work includes all one-target preprocessing, fresh randomness, failed outcomes, hashing, arithmetic, memory access, recovery, verification and output. The uniform worst-case instruction bound is 162741432569968250906303761388095885571*3420160+2^40, with all costs justified in machine.md. No prior acceptance, searched advice, amortization or actual production-scale attack execution is assumed.

experiments.purpose: Check full-width Montgomery and BN254 invariants, test the actual walk on small prime groups including failures, and reproduce the complete reduced-cap cost. These do not prove production success.
